amendments.normalized_body: The v3→v4 save migration for `reserve_g` should seed the reserve proportionally to the existing shrimp population instead of defaulting to 0.0. When an old save with an established colony (e.g. 30 adults, 20 juveniles) is loaded, `reserve_g = 0.0` causes all hatching (`fund_hatched_clutch_biomass`) and juvenile maturation (`fund_live_shrimp_biomass`) to fail until enough feeding cycles accumulate reserve. The migration function `migrate_v3_to_v4` should compute a reasonable initial reserve — e.g. `reserve_g = shrimp_biomass_g(adults, juveniles) * LIVE_BIOMASS_ORGANIC_FRACTION_G_PER_G` — so established populations don't experience a transient reproduction/growth block on upgrade.

Add an alkalinity adjustment when TAN is produced by shrimp excretion and respiration in `route_consumed_food`. When amino acids are catabolized, each mole of NH3/NH4+ released increases alkalinity by approximately 1 meq. The current code adds TAN to `ammonia_total_mg_n_total` but does not adjust `alkalinity_meq_total`. At the excretion+respiration rates in this model (excr_frac=0.10, resp_frac=0.70 of assimilated N), omitting this coupling will cause pH to drift lower than it should over time because the DIC increase from respiration suppresses pH without the counterbalancing alkalinity increase from ammonia release. Add: `state.water.alkalinity_meq_total += (excreted_n_mg + respired_n_mg) / 14.007` (converting mg N to meq NH3).

Phase 1 `reserve_g` has no maintenance drain and will grow without bound over multi-month or multi-year simulation runs. While the code comment at shrimp.rs:245-248 acknowledges this, the unbounded accumulation means the N+C budget will increasingly shift into the reserve pool. Consider adding a minimal daily maintenance drain (e.g. `reserve_g *= (1.0 - maintenance_fraction)` with maintenance_fraction as a named parameter, default ~0.01/day) that routes the drained mass to TAN+DIC via the same respiration pathway. This keeps reserve bounded, adds metabolic realism, and provides a natural hook for the later condition/molt work.

Fix `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:218-239`: `route_consumed_food` now books the full respiration fraction into DIC/TAN and only then clamps `dissolved_oxygen_mg_total` at zero. Under low-DO conditions this creates respired C/N fluxes that were never actually oxidized and undercounts the reserve that should retain the unrespired share. Respiration needs to be scaled by available O2 before routing DIC/TAN and retained reserve.

Fix `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:78-86` together with `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:242-245`: `step_daily_shrimp` now refreshes carbonate state only after `update_condition`, but `update_condition` computes NH3 toxicity from `state.water.ph`. Feeding changes TAN/DIC first, so condition, molt stress, and reproduction are all being evaluated from stale pre-feeding pH for the whole day. Recompute carbonate state immediately after `shrimp_feeding` and before the condition-dependent steps.

Revert the fallback added in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:631-670` as used by hatching at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:446-449` and maturation at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:534-536`. `fund_live_shrimp_biomass` now creates new shrimp biomass directly out of DOC/DIC/DON/TAN whenever `reserve_g` is short. That bypasses the explicit reserve pathway this bead introduced, lets juveniles hatch or mature with zero assimilated reserve, and gives shrimp an implausible ability to turn dissolved inorganic pools into tissue.

Fix `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:402-407`: `RemoveShrimp` now computes the exported reserve fraction against `adults_count` only. If all adults are removed while juveniles remain, `removed_frac` becomes 1.0 and the entire shared reserve pool is deleted. The reserve export needs to stay proportional to the whole shrimp population, or another explicit biomass share, not just adults.

Restore legacy stability-tracker reseeding in `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:179-184` and `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:350-361`. The loader no longer has access to `file_version`, so schema-v2 saves that serialized `StabilityTracker::default()` are treated as valid historical baselines instead of being reseeded. Those saves will register a fake instability swing on the first update after load.
